question:
A certain university computer laboratory hires 4 undergraduate students (code names 1, 2, 3, 4) and 2 graduate students (code names 5, 6) to provide on-duty assistance. It is known that the maximum number of duty hours that each person can be assigned from Monday to Friday, as well as the hourly duty remuneration for each person, are shown in Table 5-9.

Table 5-9:
\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c}
\hline \multirow{2}{*}{ Student Code } & \multirow{2}{*}{ Remuneration/(¥/h) } & \multicolumn{5}{|c}{ Maximum Duty Time per Day (h) } \
\cline { 3 - 7 } & & Monday & Tuesday & Wednesday & Thursday & Friday \
\hline 1 & 10.0 & 6 & 0 & 6 & 0 & 7 \
\hline 2 & 10.0 & 0 & 6 & 0 & 6 & 0 \
\hline 3 & 9.9 & 4 & 8 & 3 & 0 & 5 \
\hline 4 & 9.8 & 5 & 5 & 6 & 0 & 4 \
\hline 5 & 10.8 & 3 & 0 & 4 & 8 & 0 \
\hline 6 & 11.3 & 0 & 6 & 0 & 6 & 3 \
\hline
\end{tabular}

The laboratory is open from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM, and there must be one and only one student on duty during the opening hours. It is also stipulated that each undergraduate student must have a minimum of 8 hours of duty per week, and each graduate student must have a minimum of 7 hours of duty per week. Based on the above, the following requirements are added: firstly, each student should not have more than 2 duty shifts per week, and secondly, the number of students assigned to duty each day should not exceed 3. Based on this, establish a new mathematical model.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # students 1..6
    "students": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "undergrads": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "grads": [5, 6],
    # days 1..5 = Mon..Fri
    "days": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    # hourly remuneration (yuan/h)
    "pay": {1: 10.0, 2: 10.0, 3: 9.9, 4: 9.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 11.3},
    # max duty hours per student per day, cap[student][day]
    "cap": {
        1: {1: 6, 2: 0, 3: 6, 4: 0, 5: 7},
        2: {1: 0, 2: 6, 3: 0, 4: 6, 5: 0},
        3: {1: 4, 2: 8, 3: 3, 4: 0, 5: 5},
        4: {1: 5, 2: 5, 3: 6, 4: 0, 5: 4},
        5: {1: 3, 2: 0, 3: 4, 4: 8, 5: 0},
        6: {1: 0, 2: 6, 3: 0, 4: 6, 5: 3},
    },
    # lab open 8:00-22:00 -> 14 duty hours required per day
    "daily_hours": 14,
    # weekly minimum hours
    "min_undergrad": 8,
    "min_grad": 7,
    # at most 2 shifts (working days) per week per student
    "max_shifts": 2,
    # at most 3 students scheduled per day
    "max_students_per_day": 3,
    # big-M for the shift-indicator linking constraint
    "bigM": 100,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["students"], ordered=True)
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["days"], ordered=True)
    model.U = pyo.Set(initialize=d["undergrads"], ordered=True)
    model.G = pyo.Set(initialize=d["grads"], ordered=True)

    # x[i,j]: duty hours of student i on day j (integer, bounded by cap)
    def x_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, d["cap"][i][j])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=x_bounds)

    # z[i,j]: 1 if student i works (any hours) on day j
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # objective: minimize total weekly remuneration
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(d["pay"][i] * model.x[i, j] for i in model.I for j in model.J),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # link z -> x: x[i,j] <= cap[i,j] * z[i,j]
    def link_ub_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["cap"][i][j] * m.z[i, j]

    model.link_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.J, rule=link_ub_rule)

    # link x -> z: x[i,j] >= 1 * z[i,j]  (if scheduled, must work >= 1 h)
    def link_lb_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] >= m.z[i, j]

    model.link_lb = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.J, rule=link_lb_rule)

    # exactly daily_hours of coverage per day
    def cover_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in m.I) == d["daily_hours"]

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=cover_rule)

    # weekly minimum hours for undergraduates
    def min_under_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.J) >= d["min_undergrad"]

    model.min_under = pyo.Constraint(model.U, rule=min_under_rule)

    # weekly minimum hours for graduates
    def min_grad_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.J) >= d["min_grad"]

    model.min_grad = pyo.Constraint(model.G, rule=min_grad_rule)

    # at most max_shifts working days per student per week
    def shifts_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.z[i, j] for j in m.J) <= d["max_shifts"]

    model.shifts = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=shifts_rule)

    # at most max_students_per_day students scheduled each day
    def per_day_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.z[i, j] for i in m.I) <= d["max_students_per_day"]

    model.per_day = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=per_day_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# PROBLEM: Laboratory duty scheduling (Mon-Fri, 8:00-22:00 = 14 h/day)
#
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   x[i,d]  : hours student i works on day d          (NonNegativeReals, 0..maxhrs)
#   y[i,d]  : 1 if student i works at all on day d    (Binary)  -- shift indicator
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize total weekly remuneration)
#   sum_{i,d} remun[i] * x[i,d]
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Daily coverage: exactly 14 h of duty each day (one and only one student
#       on duty during opening hours).            sum_i x[i,d] == 14   for all d
#   (2) Daily availability cap: x[i,d] <= maxhrs[i,d] * y[i,d]  for all i,d
#   (3) Weekly minimum duty: undergrads >= 8 h, grads >= 7 h.
#   (4) At most 2 duty shifts (days) per week:  sum_d y[i,d] <= 2  for all i
#   (5) At most 3 students assigned to duty each day: sum_i y[i,d] <= 3 for all d
# =============================================================================

DATA = {
    # hourly remuneration (¥/h)
    "remun": {1: 10.0, 2: 10.0, 3: 9.9, 4: 9.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 11.3},
    # maximum duty hours per day: (student, day) -> hours ; day 1=Mon ... 5=Fri
    "maxhrs": {
        (1, 1): 6, (1, 2): 0, (1, 3): 6, (1, 4): 0, (1, 5): 7,
        (2, 1): 0, (2, 2): 6, (2, 3): 0, (2, 4): 6, (2, 5): 0,
        (3, 1): 4, (3, 2): 8, (3, 3): 3, (3, 4): 0, (3, 5): 5,
        (4, 1): 5, (4, 2): 5, (4, 3): 6, (4, 4): 0, (4, 5): 4,
        (5, 1): 3, (5, 2): 0, (5, 3): 4, (5, 4): 8, (5, 5): 0,
        (6, 1): 0, (6, 2): 6, (6, 3): 0, (6, 4): 6, (6, 5): 3,
    },
    "students": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "undergrads": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "grads": [5, 6],
    "days": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    "open_hours": 14,          # 8:00-22:00
    "ug_min_week": 8,          # undergrad weekly minimum hours
    "gr_min_week": 7,          # grad weekly minimum hours
    "max_shifts": 2,           # max duty shifts (days) per student per week
    "max_students_per_day": 3, # max students assigned to duty each day
    "bigM": 14,                # upper bound for x[i,d] (<= open_hours)
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["students"], ordered=True)
    model.D = pyo.Set(initialize=d["days"], ordered=True)
    model.UG = pyo.Set(initialize=d["undergrads"], ordered=True)
    model.GR = pyo.Set(initialize=d["grads"], ordered=True)

    # x[i,d]: hours student i works on day d
    def x_bounds(m, i, dd):
        return (0, d["maxhrs"][(i, dd)])
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, model.D, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                      bounds=x_bounds)

    # y[i,d]: 1 if student i works on day d
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, model.D, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total remuneration
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["remun"][i] * m.x[i, dd] for i in m.I for dd in m.D)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # (1) Daily coverage: exactly open_hours each day
    def coverage_rule(m, dd):
        return sum(m.x[i, dd] for i in m.I) == d["open_hours"]
    model.coverage = pyo.Constraint(model.D, rule=coverage_rule)

    # (2) Link x and y: x[i,d] <= maxhrs[i,d] * y[i,d]
    def link_rule(m, i, dd):
        return m.x[i, dd] <= d["maxhrs"][(i, dd)] * m.y[i, dd]
    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.D, rule=link_rule)

    # (3a) Undergrad weekly minimum
    def ug_min_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, dd] for dd in m.D) >= d["ug_min_week"]
    model.ug_min = pyo.Constraint(model.UG, rule=ug_min_rule)

    # (3b) Grad weekly minimum
    def gr_min_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, dd] for dd in m.D) >= d["gr_min_week"]
    model.gr_min = pyo.Constraint(model.GR, rule=gr_min_rule)

    # (4) At most max_shifts duty days per student per week
    def shifts_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.y[i, dd] for dd in m.D) <= d["max_shifts"]
    model.shifts = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=shifts_rule)

    # (5) At most max_students_per_day students assigned each day
    def per_day_rule(m, dd):
        return sum(m.y[i, dd] for i in m.I) <= d["max_students_per_day"]
    model.per_day = pyo.Constraint(model.D, rule=per_day_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# Decision variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# x[i, j] : hours assigned to student i on day j
#           i in STUDENTS = {1,...,6}, j in DAYS = {1,...,5}
#           domain: NonNegativeReals, bounds (0, max_hours[i][j])
#
# y[i, j] : binary, = 1 if student i works a duty shift on day j, else 0
#           (used to count shifts per week and enforce the <=2 shifts rule)
#
# Objective (minimize): total weekly remuneration
#           sum_{i,j} pay[i] * x[i, j]
#
# Constraints
# (1) Coverage: for each day j, total hours assigned that day must equal the
#     laboratory opening hours (8:00-22:00 = 14 h), and exactly one student is
#     on duty at any time.  Since each student works at most one contiguous
#     shift per day, requiring sum_i x[i,j] = 14 with x[i,j] <= max_hours[i][j]
#     and at most one positive x[i,j] per day models "one and only one student".
#     The "at most one positive per day" is enforced via y and big-M.
# (2) Weekly minimum hours: each undergraduate (1-4) >= 8 h/week;
#     each graduate (5-6) >= 7 h/week.
# (3) At most 2 duty shifts per week per student: sum_j y[i,j] <= 2.
# (4) At most 3 students assigned to duty each day: sum_i y[i,j] <= 3.
# (5) Linking: x[i,j] <= max_hours[i,j] * y[i,j]  (big-M with M = max_hours)
#     and x[i,j] >= 0.  Also x[i,j] <= max_hours[i,j].
# =============================================================================

DATA = {
    "students": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "undergrads": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "grads": [5, 6],
    "days": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],  # 1=Mon ... 5=Fri
    "pay": {1: 10.0, 2: 10.0, 3: 9.9, 4: 9.8, 5: 10.8, 6: 11.3},
    # max duty hours per day: max_hours[i][j]
